summary: Dominion is the original deckbuilder, where players start with a weak deck and use turns to buy better cards from a shared, rotating market to build an efficient engine before triggering the endgame. It plays fast and gives every session a distinct puzzle because the ten available Kingdom cards change each time.
praised: Endlessly replayable due to card combinations
Fast setup and clean, teachable rules
Elegant, tight design with no wasted rules
criticised: Little direct player interaction in many card sets
Can suffer analysis paralysis in the buy phase
Base set feels dated/thin compared to later expansions
Solvability of optimal strategies in some card combos

interaction.kind: racing for limited supply piles and, when attack cards are in the kingdom, directly hurting opponents' hands/decks
interaction.detail: Most of a turn is spent optimizing your own deck privately, but the shared card supply piles are finite and can run out, denying options to others, and any attack cards drafted into the game let you directly discard, curse, or slow down opponents. How interactive a given game feels depends heavily on which kingdom cards are in play that session.
interaction.said: often called "multiplayer solitaire" for its base engine-building, but attack cards (witch, militia) make it feel much more "take that" and "mean" when included

sources: Points on cards (Victory cards, Curses, and VP-granting Kingdom cards)
scoring.how_you_win: You spend turns buying cards to build an efficient deck, acquiring victory cards along the way; when the Province pile (or any 3 piles) empties, whoever has the most VP in their deck wins.
scoring.score_note: lower with more players (fewer Provinces each)
